main_body: Tall dark stone throne seen from the front: a pointed backrest with gold trim, red cushion seat, dark armrests/side blocks and a stepped dark base with a gold strip.
top_band: none. In the middle column the rows go dark backrest, gold inlay, red gem, then the red cushion at rows 18-23 (red with a pink lower band). The cushion is a vertical face seen head-on. No lighter horizontal seat surface sits above a separate front face.
evidence: The throne is drawn as a flat architectural elevation. The seat is a red cushion band (rows 18-23) painted face-on between the armrests, with only a thin gold line at the top of the arms (rows 17-18) and a gold highlight at the bottom. No seat surface is visible from above. The backrest, arms and base are all vertical faces. The seat must be seen from above, and here it is not.

style.evidence: The backrest and base are large areas of near-black and dark grey with almost no variation or grain. The outline is a neutral near-black with no material tint. The red cushion has about 3 steps and the gold trim is simple. Compared with the textured wood, tile and stone of the stall and well references, tiles here carry only 2-4 colours, so the piece looks thinner and more sticker-like.
